# Optical Dateline West Small

<div class="gc-badges">
<span class="gc-badge">raster</span><span class="gc-badge">GeoTIFF</span><span class="gc-badge">EPSG:4326</span><span class="gc-badge">tiny</span><span class="gc-badge">bundled</span>
</div>

An RGB GeoTIFF whose bounds straddle the antimeridian at -180 longitude, mirroring optical_dateline_small about 180. The control for the crossing's sign: identical size, dtype, band count, CRS and pixel size, so a behavioural difference between the pair is attributable to the direction of the crossing and to nothing else.

## What this case checks

Answer whether antimeridian mishandling is symmetric. Round 6 found GDAL's AutoCreateWarpedVRT returning a zero-height dataset for the eastward-crossing sibling and could not say whether the westward crossing behaves the same, because no negative-wrap raster existed. Run both; a difference names the sign.
